verdict.rationale: Isaac Sim has a first-party ROS 2 bridge and says it can "validate robot stacks with ROS 2" through software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop testing. Isaac ROS packages deploy to both workstations and Jetson, and Isaac Lab can package policies into a portable bundle for real hardware. Together these imply one ROS 2 stack or policy can target sim and robot, though no doc says outright "no rewrite". The community report of sim-to-real physics drift concerns behavioral fidelity, not code portability, so it lowers confidence rather than the verdict. Missing for 10: an explicit documented sim/real swap workflow (e.g., the same launch files or hardware abstraction switching between sim and robot), and independent hands-on confirmation that code runs unchanged on both.
